title: The Liver and Excretion
content:
# The Liver and Excretion

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the structure and blood supply of the liver
- Explain the role of the liver in excretion
- Describe deamination and the ornithine cycle
- Explain other functions of the liver

## Introduction

The **liver** is a vital organ with many functions, including a key role in excretion. It produces urea from excess amino acids through a process called deamination. The liver also detoxifies harmful substances and stores important nutrients.

## Key Concepts

### Liver Structure

**Location:** Upper right abdomen, below diaphragm

**Size:** Largest internal organ (~1.5 kg)

**Structure:**
- Made of liver lobules
- Lobules contain hepatocytes (liver cells)
- Rich blood supply

[DIAGRAM: Position and structure of liver]

### Blood Supply to Liver

**Unique dual blood supply:**

| Vessel | Carries | From |
|--------|---------|------|
| Hepatic artery | Oxygenated blood | Heart (via aorta) |
| Hepatic portal vein | Nutrient-rich blood | Intestines |
| Hepatic vein | Blood leaving liver | To heart (via vena cava) |

**Key point:** Portal vein brings blood directly from intestines
- Contains absorbed nutrients
- May contain toxins
- Liver processes before reaching rest of body

### Functions of the Liver

| Function | Details |
|----------|----------|
| Deamination | Converts excess amino acids to urea |
| Detoxification | Breaks down alcohol, drugs, toxins |
| Bile production | For fat digestion |
| Glycogen storage | Stores excess glucose |
| Protein synthesis | Makes plasma proteins |
| Cholesterol metabolism | Makes and breaks down cholesterol |
| Vitamin/mineral storage | Stores vitamins A, D, B12, iron |

### Deamination

**Definition:** Removal of the amino group from amino acids

**Why necessary?**
- Cannot store excess amino acids
- Cannot store excess protein
- Must remove nitrogen-containing part

**Process:**
$$\text{Amino acid} \rightarrow \text{Ammonia (NH}_3\text{)} + \text{Keto acid}$$

### What Happens to the Products?

| Product | Fate |
|---------|------|
| Ammonia | Converted to urea (less toxic) |
| Keto acid | Used in respiration OR converted to fat |

### The Ornithine Cycle (Urea Cycle)

**Purpose:** Convert toxic ammonia to less toxic urea

**Location:** Liver cells (hepatocytes)

**Overall reaction:**
$$2NH_3 + CO_2 \rightarrow \text{Urea} + H_2O$$

**Equation:**
$$2NH_3 + CO_2 \rightarrow CO(NH_2)_2 + H_2O$$

[DIAGRAM: Simplified ornithine cycle]

### Why Convert Ammonia to Urea?

| Ammonia | Urea |
|---------|------|
| Very toxic | Less toxic |
| Cannot accumulate | Can be safely transported |
| Must be diluted greatly | Less water needed |
| Would need huge urine volume | Concentrated in urine |

### Journey of Urea

1. Amino acids absorbed from intestines
2. Excess amino acids deaminated in liver
3. Ammonia converted to urea
4. Urea released into blood
5. Blood carries urea to kidneys
6. Urea filtered and excreted in urine

### Detoxification

**Definition:** Making toxic substances less harmful

**Examples:**
| Substance | How liver deals with it |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Alcohol | Converted to acetaldehyde then acetate |
| Drugs | Broken down or modified |
| Hydrogen peroxide | Converted to water by catalase |
| Hormones | Broken down when no longer needed |

### Alcohol Detoxification

**Pathway:**
$$\text{Ethanol} \xrightarrow{\text{alcohol dehydrogenase}} \text{Acetaldehyde} \xrightarrow{} \text{Acetate}$$

**Problems with excess alcohol:**
- Overwhelms liver capacity
- Damages liver cells
- Can lead to cirrhosis

### Other Liver Functions

**Glycogen storage:**
- Stores glucose as glycogen
- Releases glucose when needed
- Controlled by insulin and glucagon

**Bile production:**
- Bile made from cholesterol
- Stored in gallbladder
- Emulsifies fats in digestion

**Plasma protein synthesis:**
- Makes albumin
- Makes clotting factors
- Makes some transport proteins

### Liver Disease

| Condition | Cause | Effect |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Cirrhosis | Alcohol, hepatitis | Scarring, loss of function |
| Hepatitis | Viral infection | Inflammation |
| Fatty liver | Obesity, alcohol | Fat accumulation |
| Liver failure | Various | Cannot perform functions |

### Symptoms of Liver Disease

| Symptom | Why it occurs |
|---------|---------------|
| Jaundice (yellow skin) | Bile pigments accumulate |
| Bruising easily | Clotting factors not made |
| Confusion | Ammonia accumulates |
| Swelling | Albumin not made |

### Liver Regeneration

**Remarkable ability:**
- Liver can regenerate
- Can regrow from as little as 25%
- Allows living donor transplants
- Regeneration limited if severely damaged

## Common Exam Questions

- Describe the role of the liver in excretion
- Explain deamination and the formation of urea
- Describe the blood supply to the liver
- State other functions of the liver

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** The liver excretes urea
- **Reality:** The liver makes urea; kidneys excrete it

- **Misconception:** The liver only has one blood supply
- **Reality:** Two supplies: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein

- **Misconception:** Alcohol is excreted unchanged
- **Reality:** Liver breaks it down through detoxification

- **Misconception:** Amino acids are stored for later use
- **Reality:** Excess amino acids are deaminated (cannot be stored)

## Practice Questions

1. Name the two blood vessels that supply blood to the liver. (2 marks)

2. Define deamination. (2 marks)

3. Explain why ammonia is converted to urea. (3 marks)

4. State three functions of the liver other than making urea. (3 marks)

5. Describe what happens to excess amino acids in the body. (4 marks)

6. Describe the role of the liver in excretion. Include the processes of deamination and urea formation. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Hepatocyte | Liver cell |
| Hepatic portal vein | Vessel bringing blood from intestines to liver |
| Deamination | Removal of amino group from amino acids |
| Ornithine cycle | Pathway converting ammonia to urea |
| Urea | Less toxic nitrogenous waste |
| Detoxification | Making harmful substances less toxic |
| Cirrhosis | Scarring of liver due to damage |

## Summary

- Liver has dual blood supply: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein
- Main excretory role: making urea from excess amino acids
- Deamination removes amino group → ammonia
- Ornithine cycle converts ammonia to urea (less toxic)
- Urea transported to kidneys for excretion
- Other functions: detoxification, bile production, glycogen storage, protein synthesis
- Alcohol and drugs detoxified in liver
- Liver disease impairs these functions; can be life-threatening
